source.title: Reusing Pre-Training Data at Test Time is a Compute Multiplier
source.authors: Alex Fang; Thomas Voice; Ruoming Pang; Ludwig Schmidt; Tom Gunter

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It measures downstream benchmark accuracy across pre-training compute budgets and fits a bounded sigmoid, rather than measuring the held-out cross-entropy power laws studied in the original sources.
record.gate_note: The paper cites classical scaling-law studies but does not measure held-out pre-training loss or compute-optimal parameter/token allocations. Its relevant scaling evidence is downstream MMLU accuracy across compute budgets; Figure 1 also plots Math-500 and SimpleQA across budgets. Retrieval-method comparisons and compute-multiplier results are not evidence about the loss-scaling versions.
record.test_reason: The study pre-trains five dense models of 6.4B–77.8B parameters at about 20 tokens per parameter, spanning about two orders of compute. It reports base MMLU accuracy at each budget and fits a bounded sigmoid in log-FLOPs. That is a direct, if small, result on V6 (downstream performance improving predictably with scale). The fit is used mainly as a tool for compute-multiplier estimates. No held-out prediction or fit-quality statistic is reported, and loss is never measured, so V1–V5 and V7 are untested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that retrieving from the pre-training datasets gives large gains that survive decontamination: on MMLU, about a 4.86x average compute multiplier, declining to 2.88x at the largest scale. Adding test-time compute (reranking, self-consistency, variance reduction) yields over 11x for Llama 3.1 8B. Overall, current pre-training underuses its datasets, and the datasets themselves can be improved through better crawling and extraction.
record.recipe_differences: Measures downstream benchmark accuracy across compute budgets and fits a bounded sigmoid; it does not measure held-out cross-entropy or fit the original power-law loss relationships.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported retrieval compute multiplier varies across compute budgets and MMLU categories; retrieval gains also vary by task.

fits_no_version.finding: The compute multiplier from retrieving pre-training data falls with scale on MMLU, from 7.17x at 1.9e22 FLOPs to 2.88x at 7.34e23 FLOPs, and varies by subject category.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gains from test-time retrieval over the pre-training corpus show diminishing returns relative to pre-training compute scaling.

record.problems: The quantitative compute-scaling fit is for MMLU accuracy, not held-out pre-training loss. The paper reports five compute budgets and gives no uncertainty estimates for these results.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 1 plots base, decontaminated, subset, and full retrieval results for MMLU, Math-500, and SimpleQA across compute budgets, but does not tabulate those per-model values; these figure-only points are not extracted as separate rows. Other retrieval and test-time-compute comparisons do not test downstream predictability with pre-training scale.

untested.parts: Held-out pre-training loss is never reported.
No extrapolation from small to large runs. The sigmoid is fit in-sample on all five points; its later application to Llama 3.1 8B is a tool use, not a test.
Tokens per parameter is fixed at about 20; no compute-optimal allocation is studied.
No other modalities or regimes are scaled.

Untested parts: prediction of downstream performance from pre-training loss; out-of-sample predictive accuracy of the fitted sigmoid; goodness of fit. Base Math-500 and SimpleQA scaling appear only in Figure 1, without a fit.
Sensitivity of the fit to setup or fitting choices is not examined.

missing.what: Base-model MMLU accuracy per category (STEM, Humanities, Social, Other) at the five compute budgets, with category-specific sigmoid fit parameters; each category rises monotonically.
Base-model Math-500 and SimpleQA accuracy across the five compute budgets (figure only).
Fitted MMLU sigmoid parameters: slope 0.7968, midpoint 2.48e22 FLOPs, floor 0.25, ceiling 0.9407.

record.verdict_notes: The record treated the retrieval rows as V6 evidence; they are re-linked to none. V6 support rests on five in-sample points with no uncertainty or fit diagnostics, so it is weak evidence. The paper says it fits a 'power law' in the introduction but actually fits a bounded sigmoid.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pre-training loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether power laws fitted on small runs predict much larger runs.
The compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.
Effects of architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Scaling-law form in other modalities or training regimes.

The paper fits downstream MMLU accuracy against compute, but does not test prediction from pre-training loss. Math-500 and SimpleQA scaling curves are plotted but not numerically tabulated or fitted in the text.
Whether loss-law exponents or compute-optimal allocations depend on setup or fitting choices, or whether loss curves bend away from a power law.

relationships.condition: Base models, 6.4B–77.8B parameters at ~20 tokens/param, MMLU 5-shot, 5.64e21–7.34e23 FLOPs
relationships.reason: Base MMLU rises monotonically, 0.4873 to 0.7633, and is described by a bounded sigmoid in log-FLOPs (Table 2). Category fits behave the same way (Tables 12–15, from the text). Rows r1, r3, r5, r7, r9. No fit-quality or held-out check is reported.
relationships.display_finding: MMLU increased monotonically from 0.4873 to 0.7633 and followed bounded sigmoid fits in log FLOPs overall and by category, without held-out validation.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
